_README: Three confirmed defects, each repaired by replacing one span, each grounded in data already
in the catalog. A fourth suspected defect was REFUTED and is deliberately not touched — see
the bottom of this file, because acting on it would have made the app worse.

wa_mcclellan_peak_southwest_scramble._why: The inline sentence gave the core Enchantments overnight quota window as June 15-Oct 15. That is the PRE-2016 window — the Forest Service expanded the season by six weeks in 2016. It is stale by a decade, not a typo.
wa_mcclellan_peak_southwest_scramble._grounding: This row's own `permit` column, its `access.permit`, its `access.notes` and its `itinerary.cal` all already say May 15-Oct 31, as does every peer row across the Enchantments that carries a permit string. The inline sentence was the lone outlier in the whole area.

set.approach: From Leavenworth, drive Icicle Road (Forest Road 7600) about 4.2–4.3 miles west to the Snow Lakes Trailhead and parking area on the south side of the road (~1,350 ft). Start on the Snow Lakes Trail No. 1553, which climbs steadily through forest along Icicle Creek/Snow Creek drainage. Around 4 miles in you pass Nada Lake, with a loud waterfall/creek blast just above it that's a reliable water source; continue to Lower and Upper Snow Lakes, where a logjam between the two lakes is a known crossing hazard (especially at high water or in the dark on an alpine start). Beyond the Snow Lakes the trail (now a rougher climbers' path) switchbacks steeply up into the core Enchantments basin, passing Lake Viviane, then Leprechaun and Sprite Lakes — by this point you've covered roughly 9–10 miles and gained most of the route's elevation. At the flat, open area at ~7,000 ft between Leprechaun and Sprite Lakes, leave the maintained trail and head south-southeast, aiming for McClellan Ridge and staying west of a distinctive rock tower known as "the Prong." Ascend steep talus, scree, or snow (depending on season — often firm/icy in late summer and fall, so an axe/microspikes are worth carrying) to gain the ridge crest. This upper section has no reliable water and involves real route-finding; a permit is required to camp overnight in the core Enchantments zone (May 15-Oct 31).

wa_upper_castle_toprope_wall._why: The approach column opened with a research memo — 'Note on data: the only real-world crag called Upper Castle...' — arguing about whether the row was misfiled under Mount Rainier. That question is already settled: the row's own data_quality.gaps records the reassignment to wa_upper_castle in 2026-07, and it now sits beside 33 genuine Upper Castle routes. Only the last two sentences of the field were an approach at all. This is prose-in-a-display-field of exactly the class the repo warns about.
wa_upper_castle_toprope_wall._grounding: This route's own researched approach_variants, and the same approach carried independently by peer rows in wa_upper_castle.

set.approach: Castle Rock stands beside US-2 in Tumwater Canyon, about two to two and a half miles west of Leavenworth, with an oversized dirt pullout on the north side of the highway around milepost 96.5. park in the pullout/parking area in Tumwater Canyon along US-2, and take the climbers' trail starting on the west side of the lot. The trail climbs east across a broad ledge feature called Logger's Ledge, splitting the formation; the first routes are reachable in about 5-10 minutes of easy uphill walking. There's no named trail number and no water source at the crag — bring what you need.

wa_enchantment_peak_southwest_scramble._why: The descent opened by telling the party to downclimb the SW summit's exposed, needle-like final block, about 25 ft of narrow class 4. But this row states its own scope repeatedly — its overview says it approaches THE NE SUMMIT from the southwest and explicitly not the technical SW pinnacle, and its rock_grade calls the low-5th option onto the SW sub-summit not required. So a route graded Class 2-3 was instructing a class 4 downclimb it never climbed. The SW fin is a separate side-trip along the crest, roughly 1,500 ft away, and is not this route's descent.
wa_enchantment_peak_southwest_scramble._grounding: This row's own overview, rock_grade and watch_out fields, plus the peer row wa_enchantment_peak_east_ridge, which names the two routes on this peak by APPROACH SIDE rather than by summit.

set.descent_text: Reverse the ascent line. This route tops out on the NORTHEAST summit, which a 2023 survey confirms is the true high point, and its descent is a walk-off: downclimb the short, loose 3rd-class gully off the summit plateau — the same step you came up — then reverse the cross-country traverse back through the Reginleif/Sigrun tarn basin to the top of Aasgard Pass. Downclimbing Aasgard Pass is the descent's main hazard: steep, loose talus that's arguably harder to descend than ascend — plunge-step or downclimb deliberately and stay off snow you can't see the run-out on. Do not glissade the snow-filled sections of Aasgard Pass; several serious and fatal accidents have occurred there from glissaders sliding into hidden moats and sub-snow meltwater channels, especially in early-to-mid season. From the base of the pass, follow the Colchuck Lake shoreline and the Colchuck Lake Trail / Stuart Lake Trail back to the Stuart Lake Trailhead. This is a walk-off/downclimb route overall — no established rappels on the standard line.

_REFUTED.wa_little_annapurna_south_slopes: Reported as 'aspect N/NW contradicts a route named South Slopes'. REFUTED, and the inversion runs the other way: the ASPECT IS CORRECT and the NAME is wrong. The row's own `face` says north/west-facing slopes near the northeast ridge; its own waypoint for the 'base of south slopes' sits NORTH of the summit, so the ascent travels southward up a north-facing slope; the peer row wa_little_annapurna_south_face is the peak's genuine south side, a 5.6 technical face reached from Ingalls Creek, a different valley entirely; and it is published as 'Little Annapurna North Slope'. NOT TOUCHED, because 'fixing' the aspect to S would have broken a currently CORRECT sun/shade readout — turning a shady north slog into a sunny one. The real repair is renaming the route and inverting the N/S words in its prose (its hazards warn you off 'the abrupt north-side drop' when the drop is on the SOUTH), and a rename is an identity change that wants a human.
_REFUTED.wa_upper_castle_toprope_wall_road: Second defect on that row, same root cause, NOT fixed here: its `road` column still holds the Mount Rainier value — 'Nisqually-Paradise Road (SR 706 to Paradise)' with drive directions from Seattle through Elbe to the Nisqually Entrance. It is the ONLY row in wa_upper_castle with `road` populated, so there is no peer to copy from; it wants either a US-2 / Tumwater Canyon value or a null.
_REFUTED.wa_mcclellan_peak_dist_km: dist_km is 38.6 (24 mi) while the approach text describes ~9-10 miles in and the row's own itinerary calls it a ~24 mi car-to-car ROUND TRIP. So the round trip is stored in a column the app renders by doubling. NOT normalised: dist_km holds two conventions in this catalog and bulk-fixing it is forbidden. Also unreconciled on that row: obj_haz says ~18 miles, a third figure.
